422.description: Invalid gateway URL, or a client or model the route does not support

draining.description: Whether the account refuses new assignments while honoring existing model pins.

remaining_pins.description: Nonretired model pins that still have account, grant, route, pool, and key enrollment. Transient capacity and health are not counted against this total.

last_activity_at.description: Latest recorded Code Mode routing decision for this account, or null if none.

extra_usage_enabled.description: Whether the member Extra Usage paid fallback setting is on for a Kimi Code account, recorded by the operator at enrollment. Null means not recorded. It is never spare included allowance.

grant_state.description: Grant authority is independent of serving health and allowance. A rejected refresh lapses the grant and requires enrollment again.

health_observed_at.description: Time of the latest serving health observation. Enrollment and refresh do not qualify serving health.

unavailable_until.description: End of the serving cooldown. Exhausted allowance and grant authority remain independent eligibility requirements.

cooldowns.description: Live failure class cooldowns for this account. A null model cools the whole credential.

cycle_anchor.description: Operator recorded subscription cycle anchor date for Qwen Token Plan accounts. The monthly quota reset is the next monthly anniversary of this date. Null when no anchor is recorded, and no reset is reported then.

allowance_read_requested_at.description: When an operator last requested an active allowance read. The worker clears it once that read completes.

allowance_read_at.description: When the worker last completed an active allowance read for this account, whether or not the provider response was usable.

adapter.description: The subscription family of the account's provider profile: Codex, Claude, OpenCode Go, GLM Coding Plan, MiniMax M Plan, Kimi Code or Qwen Token Plan. Null for a profile no code-mode adapter serves. A pool may mix families; each request reaches an account whose family serves its path and model.

allowance_signal.description: Allowance signal qualification of the account's provider profile. Passive signals may be recorded, but no requested-model-to-limit mapping is qualified for ordering. Active reads require separate live qualification. Remains-unqualified names a signal that has not completed qualification. None means the profile has no qualified allowance signal.

allowance_signal_reason.description: Why the allowance signal is not qualified, or null when no reason is recorded.

research_eligible.description: Current research enrollment eligibility, independent of inference health and allowance; route pool membership is also required.

research_services.description: Research services supported by the enrolled profile; also requires research eligibility and route pool membership.

model.description: The model this cooldown cools, or null when it cools the whole credential.

extra_usage_enabled.description: Whether the member Extra Usage paid fallback setting is on for a Kimi Code account, recorded by the operator at enrollment. Null means not recorded. It is never spare included allowance and is refused for other adapters.

cycle_anchor.description: Optional subscription cycle anchor date, recorded only for Qwen Token Plan accounts.

CodeAttempt.description: Metadata only. No request or response body, tools, headers or secrets are retained. Reserved tokens are conservative bounds, not reported usage; unreported consumption remains uncertain indefinitely. Cached and reasoning tokens are subsets.

upstream_status.description: Observed upstream HTTP or WebSocket error status; null when not observed.

outcome.description: Bounded transport or generation result, independent of usage settlement and durable uncertainty.

operation.description: The operation the request performed: `responses`, `compact` or `prewarm` on the Responses API, `messages` on Anthropic Messages, or `chat` on Chat Completions.

allowance_charge.description: Validated per-request OpenCode Go billing and numeric usage fields, with usage.cost when reported. The allowance value counts toward plan usage limits in dollars of the monthly limit. Null means no supported charge was observed; it is never a remaining allowance and never an admission or ordering input.

end_user_digest.description: Project-scoped end-user HMAC, or empty when identification was not configured. Raw identifiers are never retained.

requested_model.description: Public model requested before explicit alias resolution.

initial_recovery.description: The portable initial input permitted recovery when admitted. False also includes historical attempts without that evidence. This does not establish account eligibility or permission to replay.

nonexecution.description: A bounded upstream rejection was verified to prove this attempt did not execute. False means nonexecution was not proven.

recovery_from.description: Prior attempt this admission recovered from, within the same project, route and API key. Null when no visible recovery source was recorded.

recovery_reason.description: Reason from the recovery source that durably proved nonexecution. Null means historical evidence is unavailable or no recovery source exists. Never inferred from current account health.

codex_cli_identity_enabled.description: Whether the frozen route revision enabled Codex CLI identity compatibility. This is route policy, not evidence that an Originator header changed or that this attempt used Codex. No client identity header values or prompt content are recorded.

CodeDecision.description: Content-free account selection record for one admitted attempt or one WebSocket connection bind. Names the chosen account, why it served, the freshest allowance evidence kind behind it, and the class reason each other candidate was skipped. No prompt, response, header or credential content is retained.

attempt_id.description: Attempt this decision admitted. Null for connection decisions, which bind a WebSocket connection to the tree account without admitting an attempt.

reason.description: Chosen means weighted selection picked the account for a new pin, pin means an established conversation pin served without re-running selection, and connection means the tree connection account served.

class.description: Why the candidate did not serve: cooldown means a live health cooldown, busy means the account reached its local generation cap, unavailable means reported allowance exhaustion, tree means an earlier account of the conversation tree served, and weight means the weighted score picked another account of the same tier.

skipped.description: Candidates evaluated alongside the chosen account that did not serve, each with the class reason it lost. Covers the evaluated candidate set only. Accounts excluded earlier by model, path or tree-adapter SQL filters are not listed.

recovery_envelope.description: Proven not-executed rejection envelope this admission recovered from. Null when the admission was not a recovery.

CodeBinding.description: Persistent per-key conversation tree identity. Retiring any member retires the whole tree; retirement never permits re-binding to another account. Account and principal are the tree's first account, which later models prefer; pins name the account each model is served from.

pins.description: The tree's pins, oldest first. A tree's first admission of a model pins an account to it, and the pin never moves.

CodeBudget.description: Optional hard token caps. Both periods use UTC. All matching attempts in the period count, including earlier usage and uncertainty. Disabling does not release reservations. Route/key scope cannot change.

adapters.description: The subscription families whose accounts serve the client's published models and exact aliases, in display order. A mixed route's configuration draws each model from its own family. Empty for paid-only setup.

client.description: The client the configuration is for.

file.description: Where to merge the configuration or save the shell setup. Follow instructions to preserve existing settings.

format.description: Codex TOML, a POSIX shell or PowerShell setup to source, or OpenCode JSON.

model.description: The published model or exact alias the client uses for its main conversation.

native_models.description: The route's models an adapter supporting the client serves, in route order.

plan_model.description: The published model or exact alias for planning: Claude Code's plan mode through opusplan and OpenCode's plan agent. It equals model unless another was chosen. Null for Codex.

revision.description: The published Code Mode route revision number.

revision_id.description: The ID of the published route revision used to generate the configuration.

small_model.description: The published model or exact alias for background requests: Claude Code's Haiku-class and OpenCode's small model. Null for Codex.

supported_clients.description: The clients the route's adapters have configurations for; the first, a client of the first model's adapter, is the default.

additional_files.description: Companion configuration files required by this setup. Merge entries with existing client settings and MCP servers.

instructions.description: Platform-specific setup and merge instructions. Preserve unrelated client settings and retain environment references for credentials.

models.description: The same live route model and protocol catalog returned by the route models endpoint.

CodePin.description: The account a conversation tree serves one model from.

target_model.description: Durably pinned native model identifier. Existing native pins use their model identifier.

account_weights.description: Relative weights keyed by assigned account ID. Omitted accounts use weight 1.
Relative weights keyed by assigned account ID. Omitted accounts use weight 1.

end_user_digest.description: Project-scoped end-user HMAC, or empty when identification was not configured. Raw identifiers are never retained.

CodeRoute.description: Dedicated coding contract. Base path is /code/{slug}. Native model identifiers remain unchanged by default. Exact aliases require explicit model rewriting. Draft writes do not change the immutable runtime release. Publication does no inference. Enabled is independent of ordinary provider activation.

adapters.description: The adapters the latest published revision serves, in display order, derived from the provider connections it froze. Together they select the route's ingress paths and supported clients: Codex serves `responses`; OpenCode Go serves `v1/chat/completions`, `v1/messages` and `v1/responses`; GLM Coding Plan, MiniMax M Plan, Kimi Code and Qwen Token Plan serve `v1/messages` and `v1/chat/completions`. Each request reaches an account whose adapter serves its path and that lists its model. Empty before publication or when the revision's accounts name no adapter.

max_body_bytes.description: Optional ingress limit in bytes. Null inherits installation limits; a route can only lower them. Checks both encoded and decoded JSON, the complete multipart body, and individual client WebSocket messages. Published revisions pin this policy.

messages_to_codex.description: Explicitly allow Messages text and tool requests to use Codex subscription accounts through protocol translation. Published revisions pin this policy. Native forwarding remains the default. Translation alone preserves client identity and prompts. Codex identity compatibility requires its separate codex_cli_identity opt-in. Model rewriting requires its separate opt-in. Explicit low, medium and high reasoning effort is supported. Signed thinking, numeric reasoning budgets, beta features and unsupported required semantics are refused before dispatch.

aliases.description: Stable public model names mapped directly to one native identifier in models. Requires model_rewriting. Alias chains and native name collisions are rejected. Immutable publications pin these mappings. Repointing an alias affects new conversations. Existing conversations retain their stored exact target while it remains published and authorized.

model_rewriting.description: Explicitly enable model identifier rewriting through exact aliases or configured model_pools. Disabled by default. This policy does not rewrite client identity or prompts.

initial_recovery_attempts.description: Maximum additional attempts per request for a new or established single-pin root conversation after an adapter proves nonexecution and the complete input is portable. Zero disables recovery. Published revisions pin this policy. Existing children, socket ownership and unresolved attempts prevent migration. Exact models remain the default. Only explicit model_pools authorize model changes. Live authority remains required. Producing-account reference ownership is preserved. Accepted, partial, ambiguous and opaque work never replays.

model_pools.description: Explicit subscription model recovery pools keyed by a published native name or exact alias. Requires model_rewriting. Each ordered list starts with that name's normal exact target and contains distinct native identifiers from models. Recovery prefers the pinned exact target, then these alternatives, within initial_recovery_attempts and positive nonexecution, portability, live authorization and budget checks. Omitted pools preserve exact selection. Publications freeze the policy. Existing conversations retain their exact target, including after alias changes, while it remains published and authorized. Paid fallback is separately governed.

paid_participation.description: Explicitly permit metered API targets. Direct selection and subscription-first fallback require their separate target maps.

paid_targets.description: Exact native model to directly selected published metered provider and credential slot. A mapped model takes precedence over subscription accounts.

chat_to_antigravity.description: Explicitly allow Chat Completions text and function tools through the internal Antigravity Gemini target over HTTP or SSE. Published revisions pin this policy. Native forwarding remains the default. Client identity and prompts are preserved. Signed thought state, reasoning controls, media and server tools are unsupported. Returned signature state is refused before actionable output rather than discarded. Controlled fixtures do not qualify any current model or live subscription workflow.

paid_fallback_targets.description: Explicit native model to published metered provider and credential slot for subscription-first bounded recovery. Requires paid_participation and positive initial_recovery_attempts. Subscription candidates are preferred. Same-model fallback needs no model pool. Different models require model_rewriting and a model_pool. Proven nonexecution and complete-input portability are required. Direct paid_targets retain precedence and cannot overlap this map. Existing paid owners stay pinned. Unknown paid money remains held against applicable limits.

codex_cli_identity.description: Explicit route-administrator opt-in, disabled by default and independent of protocol translation. On Codex subscription HTTP and WebSocket requests only, fills Originator with codex_cli_rs when every supplied Originator value is absent or blank. Preserves explicit Originator values, User-Agent, all prompts, tools, reasoning, state and other headers. Does not enable translation or prompt changes. Publication freezes the policy. Using subscription accounts through this compatibility identity may violate provider terms and risk account suspension. Review this behavior and risk before enabling and publishing.

chat_to_codex.description: Explicit Chat text and function tool translation through Codex Responses, disabled by default and pinned by publication. Native forwarding remains the default. Low, medium and high reasoning effort is supported. Required signed reasoning, media, server-owned state and unsupported semantics are refused. Independent Codex identity and model rewriting policies remain separate. Current OpenCode client and live subscription acceptance remain unqualified.

CodeTokenWindows.description: Persistent reservations charged to this budget. Admission also includes matching attempts made before the budget was enabled; these window counters do not represent subscription allowance or currency.

CodeAllowance.description: Provider-reported subscription metadata. Unknown values remain null and never become local hard budgets or billed spend.

windows.description: Independent provider windows keyed by limit_id and window. Partial observations merge without replacing newer observations for another window.

CodeCountObservation.description: Observation and reset of one provider count limit, independent of other counts and percentage windows.

unit.description: Vendor unit of the reported values. Percent windows report used and remaining percentages; other units report used and remaining values in that unit.

evidence.description: How the observation was learned: passive from a forwarded response, or active from a provider usage read.

used_value.description: Used amount in the vendor unit for non-percent windows. Null when the provider did not report it.

remaining_value.description: Remaining amount in the vendor unit for non-percent windows. Null when the provider did not report it.

CodeCredits.description: Provider-reported credits. Informational: absence of add-on credits does not imply exhaustion of subscription windows, and credits do not override an exhausted window. Balance is a bounded decimal string, not inferred spend.

CodeClientPlatform.description: Developer platform for paths and shell syntax. Linux and macOS use POSIX shells, Windows uses PowerShell.

CodeModel.description: A published model currently reachable through eligible accounts in the route pool.

model_pool.description: Configured ordered subscription recovery targets for this public model. This is policy metadata, not an availability or portability guarantee. Omitted for exact-model selection.

paid.description: This model has an authorized metered API target, selected directly or through explicit fallback. Paid attempts require monetary admission.
